title: RECITE: Revising Eligibility Criteria Incorporating Textual Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2610.41368v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Overly restrictive eligibility criteria contribute to widespread enrollment failure in clinical trials, yet published recommendations for how specific criteria should be broadened remain disconnected from trial design at scale. We introduce RECITE (Revising Eligibility Criteria Incorporating Textual Evidence), a framework for automated discovery, extraction, and implementation of evidence-based eligibility criteria revisions. RECITE uses protocol amendment documents from ClinicalTrials.gov to construct a dataset of 11,913 curated instances across 5,735 trials, each pairing original criteria with documentary evidence and target revisions. We benchmark fifteen LLM configurations under truncated-to-context-window and retrieval-augmented generation conditions, on a 3,116-instance sample under an LLM-as-judge protocol validated against ten domain experts (judge vs. human quadratic-weighted Cohen's $\kappa_{qw} = 0.694 \pm 0.096$). translated_title: RECITE：结合文本证据修订资格标准
translated_abstract: 过于严格的资格标准导致临床试验中普遍存在的入组失败问题，然而已发表的关于如何放宽特定标准的建议与大规模的试验设计相脱节。我们提出了RECITE（Revising Eligibility Criteria Incorporating Textual Evidence，结合文本证据修订资格标准），这是一个用于自动化发现、提取和实施基于证据的资格标准修订的框架。RECITE利用ClinicalTrials.gov的试验方案修订文档，构建了一个涵盖5,735项试验的11,913个精选实例的数据集，每个实例都将原始资格标准与文档证据和目标修订配对。我们在截断至上下文窗口和检索增强生成两种条件下，对十五种大语言模型配置进行了基准测试，测试基于3,116个实例的样本，并采用经十位领域专家验证的“LLM作为评判者”协议（评判模型与人类之间的二次加权Cohen's κ_qw = 0.694 ± 0.096）。最佳的op（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出RECITE框架，利用ClinicalTrials.gov的方案修订文档构建了涵盖5,735项试验的11,913个实例数据集，实现了临床试验资格标准的自动化循证修订，并通过与领域专家高度一致的LLM评判协议对十五种大语言模型配置进行了基准评估。
en_tdlr: RECITE is a framework for automated discovery, extraction, and implementation of evidence-based clinical trial eligibility criteria revisions, built on a dataset of 11,913 curated instances from 5,735 trials derived from ClinicalTrials.gov protocol amendment documents, benchmarked across fifteen LLM configurations with an expert-validated LLM-as-judge protocol.
